22. Any correspondence between GGAT and Cotswold Archaeological Trust concerning the archaeological potential, results, interpretation, extent or recording of the Great House Farm site.
23. Any records showing whether the 1990 GGAT trench plan, archaeological potential map, appendices or conclusions were used to determine the location, extent or methodology of the 1994 excavation.
24. Any records identifying any material change between GGAT's 1990 assessment and the findings of the 1994 excavation, including any contemporary acknowledgment within GGAT's records that the 1994 findings differed materially from the conclusions
 or zoning of the 1990 assessment.
Part E — The 1994 Cotswold Archaeological Trust excavation archive
25. Any records held by Heneb concerning the surviving archive of the 1994 Great House Farm excavation, including information on where the archive was deposited or transferred.
26. Any records showing the date, destination and scope of any transfer or deposit of the 1994 excavation archive, including:

finds;human-remains records;context sheets;plans and drawings;photographs;catalogues;databases; andspecialist reports.
27. The published excavation record states that 1,026 inhumation burials were examined, whereas the current Heneb HER record states
858 inhumations.
Please provide any records held by Heneb which explain the difference between these figures, including whether they represent different stages of excavation, different archaeological categories, different counting methodologies, or subsequent correction
 or revision of the HER.
28. Any records showing whether material from the 1994 excavation remains with Heneb/GGAT, Cotswold Archaeology, Amgueddfa Cymru/National Museum Wales, RCAHMW, the Archaeology Data Service or another repository.
29. I understand that archive material relating to the 1994 excavation was deposited in or around 2014. Please confirm whether this is correct and, if so, provide the relevant accession/deposit information and identify the repository concerned.
Part F — Archive management following the 1983 fire
30. Any records concerning the archive-management arrangements implemented by GGAT following the 1983 fire for the preservation, cataloguing, duplication, storage and eventual deposition of excavation archives, photographs and associated
 records.
31. Any records showing whether records affected by the fire were reconstructed, recreated, copied, replaced or otherwise restored, and which archaeological projects were affected by any such work.
32. Any records concerning subsequent reviews of the completeness of excavation archives affected by the fire.
33. Any retention schedules, disposal schedules, archive policies, accession procedures or records-management guidance used by GGAT during the relevant period which governed the retention or disposal of archaeological project records and
 photographs.
Part G — Present completeness and custody of the archaeological record
34. Any surviving GGAT/Heneb records identifying missing, lost, destroyed, separated or otherwise unaccounted-for archive components relating to either the Llandough Farm excavation or Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr.
35. Any records showing whether the 1978–79 Llandough excavation archive, the 1990 Great House Farm assessment and the 1994 Great House Farm excavation archive were ever cross-referenced, reconciled or treated as related archaeological records.
36. Any records identifying discrepancies between the historical GGAT records, the present Heneb HER, the National Monuments Record of Wales and the published archaeological reports concerning these sites.
Part H — Heneb's statutory HER role and custody of information
37. Please identify the legal and administrative basis on which Heneb maintains the relevant Historic Environment Record on behalf of the Welsh Ministers, including any agreement, contract, service specification, grant agreement, memorandum
 of understanding or other instrument governing that arrangement.
38. Does Heneb consider that information forming part of the statutory Historic Environment Record is held:
a. by Heneb in its own capacity;
b. by Heneb on behalf of the Welsh Ministers; or
c. on some other legal or administrative basis?
Please explain.
39. Where historical GGAT material now held by Heneb forms evidence supporting a statutory HER record, please identify whether the underlying source archive is regarded as part of the HER itself, associated reference material, or a separate
 archaeological archive.
40. If any of the information requested above is held by Heneb solely on behalf of the Welsh Ministers, please identify the relevant Welsh Government/Cadw body responsible for access to that information and the applicable access regime.
Searches and records no longer held
I appreciate that some historical records may no longer survive.
Where information requested above is no longer held, please state that clearly and, where recorded information exists concerning its destruction, disposal, transfer, loss or separation, please provide that information.
For each material category where the original record is no longer held, please provide any surviving record showing:

when it ceased to be held;why it ceased to be held;whether it was destroyed, lost, transferred or otherwise disposed of;whether any replacement, copy or reconstruction was made; andthe repository or organisation to which it was transferred, where applicable.
If Heneb's searches establish that a record formerly known to exist cannot now be located, please identify the relevant search terms, archive locations or record systems searched and the outcome of those searches, insofar as such information is itself recorded.
Where records have been transferred to another body, please identify that body together with any accession, archive or reference number known to Heneb.
Scope and cost

the scale and nature of the archaeological and photographic losses in the March 1983 warehouse fire;what material from the 1978–79 Llandough excavation survived;the complete custody history of the 1990 Great House Farm assessment and its appendices;the relationship between that assessment and the 1994 excavation;the whereabouts and completeness of the 1994 excavation archive; andthe present accuracy and provenance of the relevant HER records.
If some information is already publicly available or is held by another body, please identify the relevant repository and, where possible, provide the relevant archive, accession or catalogue reference rather than simply directing me to the organisation
 generally.
This request is made in the public interest and is intended to establish the documentary record. It should not be read as an allegation that any individual or institution acted dishonestly, in bad faith, corruptly, or deliberately destroyed or concealed

Dear Requester,

Thank you for your email received into our enquiries system 8th September.  Please find below answers to your questions in turn.  Please note that prices quoted are without VAT based on the fact that you are in Patagonia.

**26 May 2026 (2026/2370)**
1. 1974 demolition petition, Llandough juxta Penarth — ref or not held.
There is not a petition held within our collection. You would need to know who the petition was submitted to in order to search for any further reference to it.  If it was submitted to the planning authority there may be mention in the Planning Committee minutes and reports – see point 6 below.

**29 May 2026 FOIA/EIR (2026/2372)**

2. Williams/Buckler as owners, tenants, or reporters of the 1880 floor discovery.
One source of information about ownership would be rate books. UC/73/1 is a rate book for 1882 – this is the nearest we have to 1880.  A search of this (and later volumes UC/73/1-5 covers 1882-1902 and then UDPE/T/30 and UDPE/T/32 cover dates after 1900) could be undertaken by staff on your behalf at a charge of £50 which would include copies of relevant entries.

3. Gaps / missing volumes / withdrawals 1950–1989.
We have never had a full set of records that would show the full tenancy/ownership history of Great House / Ty Mawr Farm. With all historical research of this nature, it is necessary to piece together information from surviving records that have been deposited with us.  There are not any records that have been withdrawn from our collections that would have provided additional information to this search for the period 1950-1989.

4. Why the fabric was not scheduled before 1988 (or “Cadw holds this; we hold nothing”).
Not held in our collections – suggest contacting Cadw and the Royal Commission on the Ancient and Historical Monuments of Wales.

5. Internal preservation assessments.
As above - suggest contacting Cadw and the Royal Commission on the Ancient and Historical Monuments of Wales.

6. Planning files for this acreage / demolition / Church View Close — file refs, not class names.
We do not hold planning files (it is possible some files may still be held by the Vale of Glamorgan Council Planning Department), but we do hold copies of the Planning Committee minutes and reports.  Mary Buckler started looking at the Planning Committee minutes and reports on her last visit to the searchroom on 13th August.  The document references to start with for these would be DCVG/C/4/36/76-77 and DCVG/C/4/36/94 these are for the planning applications 1989/01396/OUT and 1992/00671/RES.  It is possible that the minutes may make reference to any earlier applications or discussions.  A search of these records and anything else that they lead to could be carried out by staff at a charge of £50 to include copies of any relevant pages found.

7. When the known archaeology was raised in planning.
If any record of this is in our collections it would appear in the Planning Committee records described above in point 6.

8. EIAs / HER / developer briefs 1980–1990.
The HER for Wales is searchable via the Heneb website: Historic Environment Records (HER) - Heneb<https://heneb.org.uk/historic-environment-records-her/>.  You could also contact the Glamorgan Gwent Archaeological Trust to see if they have any relevant information.

**27 July / 5 August 2026 (2026/3309)**
9. DB/E/1–2 Stewart survey / Cedfin.
This was consulted and photographed by Mary Buckler in our public searchroom.  If you would like to receive copies of the pages relating to Ty Mawr this would be two images (one from DB/E/1 the survey and one from DB/E/2 the terrier).  Total cost £17 (£13 for the first image in the order and £4 for the next image).

10. Lambert Williams–Bute agreements 1818–1835 (not the D160 maps already seen).
Not held. Possibly at the National Library of Wales?

11. Material related to NLW D219.
Not held – this is a National Library of Wales reference: Llandough manorial leases and agreements, - National Library of Wales Archives and Manuscripts<https://archives.library.wales/index.php/llandough-manorial-leases-and-agreements> You should contact the NLW for access or copies.

12. D153/4–8 1876 limeworks severance — not seen.
Not held – this is a National Library of Wales reference: Deeds relating to premises in p. Llandough, co. Glam., comprising a dwelling house adjoining the churchyard, 1811 (D153/1-2), land (19 ..., - National Library of Wales Archives and Manuscripts<https://archives.library.wales/index.php/deeds-relating-to-premises-in-p-llandough-co-glam-comprising-dwelling-house-adjoining-churchyard-1811-d153-1-2-land-19>.  You should contact the NLW for access or copies.

13. DXJF/64/27–32 full sketch bundle — notes seen; confirm sketches and refs.
We believe that the specific references within the bundle 27-32 that would be of interest to you are items DXJF/64/30-31: sketch of former layout of part of village of Llandough-juxta-Penarth by Mrs. Nancy Buckler of great house farm, Llandough, with notes c1950 [1 card, 1 paper]. Is that what you have already seen?  Other items in the bundle do not relate to Llandough.

14. DCOWHS on Buckler of Penarth (not DCO/WHS/2).
DCOWHS/2 is the only part of the DCOWHS (Cowbridge and District Local History Society) that relates to Buckler of Penarth. No other records held.

15. Exact ref of the Nov 1877 counterpart already photographed; separate July 1877 counterpart?
I think the items described below have been discussed previously – are these what you are seeking?  Please confirm and we can provide a quote for producing copies if required.

Document reference

  *   DBDT/1/3
Title

  *   Adamsdown Square leases from the trustees of the will of the late Marquess of Bute<https://glamorgan.epexio.com/en/records/DBDT/1-110/1>. Lease to Mr John Williams
Level of description

  *   Item

Level of description

16. Cardiff RDC records for this farm.
No records found. The area was not covered by Cardiff Rural District Council but rather Penarth Urban District Council.

17. DRA 418–420 / DRA 5/31 if this site.
Neither of these are complete document references from our collection.  Perhaps you could check these references or let us know what you think they should be and we will be happy to search our catalogue.

18. UDPE/S/1/68.
This was viewed by Mary Buckler on 6th August and is a set of plans for a pair of semi-detached houses on the road between Dinas Powys and Llandough. If you would like copies of these plans 5 images will be required at a charge of £20.

19. Penarth estate/tithe/OS/boundary plans of the house plot (not Cowbridge 1924/38).
The relevant estate map would be the Bute Estate survey which is referred to in point 9 above.  You can view the tithe map online here: Tithe Maps of Wales<https://places.library.wales/viewer/4622411#?cv=&h=95&xywh=10530%2C8509%2C3549%2C1196> along with the accompanying apportionment: Tithe Maps of Wales<https://places.library.wales/viewer/4542756#?cv=1&h=95&xywh=-507%2C-68%2C2508%2C897>.  Many historic Ordnance Survey maps can also be viewed online, for example through the National Library of Scotland website: Map Finder - with Outlines - National Library of Scotland<https://maps.nls.uk/geo/find/#zoom=15.3&lat=51.45225&lon=-3.20017&layers=101&b=1&z=0&point=51.44624,-3.20044&i=135196558>.

The only relevant papers we have are those mentioned in point 5.4 in my email of 7th September: collection reference D696 – book of plans and rental books for land owned by Western Ground Rents Ltd c1938-1944.  A search of these records could be carried out on your behalf at a charge of £50.

21. Associated bundles stored separately.
All catalogues have been searched for your enquiry.

22. Uncatalogued / recent deposits 1875–1988.
A search of our accessions database, which records all records received into our collection even if they haven’t yet been catalogued, has not revealed any additional records.

23. Photography for copies to Patagonia — rules.
Please find attached the digital photography order form which applies wherever you are based.  As mentioned above, prices quoted do not include VAT due to your location.  You need to sign and agree to the declaration on the order form.

These points were answered in my email of 7th September.

These points were answered in my email of 14th September.

We hope that this information is of use to you.  We will respond to other outstanding emails in due course.

Yours sincerely,

Louise Hunt

Index of proprietors’ names

Under rule 11 of the Land Registration Rules 2003 the registrar is required to keep an index of proprietors’ names which shows for each individual register the proprietor of the registered estate and the proprietor of any registered charge together with the title number. When you search the index of proprietors’ names, you will receive a list of titles that are owned by, or mortgaged to, the name that you have searched against.

Section 21 FOIA exemption: Information accessible to the applicant by other means

Where information held on the register of title is available for inspection through these statutory routes of access it is exempt from disclosure under section 21(2)(b) of FOIA.

Section 21 states:

“21 Information accessible to applicant by other means.

(1) Information which is reasonably accessible to the applicant otherwise than under section 1 is exempt information.

(2) For the purposes of subsection (1)—

(a) information may be reasonably accessible to the applicant even though it is accessible only on payment, and

(b) information is to be taken to be reasonably accessible to the applicant if it is information which the public authority or any other person is obliged by or under any enactment to communicate (otherwise than by making the information available for inspection) to members of the public on request, whether free of charge or on payment.”

Therefore, we are unable to provide information held on our register through FOIA, as it covered by this exemption.

Register information and your data protection rights

Data protection law permits HM Land Registry to use personal data for our official purposes.

The lawful basis for HM Land Registry processing personal data under the United Kingdom (UK) General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) is that it is necessary to enable us to perform our public task of the registration of land and property (Article 6(1)(e) of UK GDPR). This is defined in the Land Registration Act 2002.

Paragraph 5 of Schedule 2 Part 1 of the Data Protection Act 2018 provides the following exemption from the specified UK GDPR provisions:

“The listed UK GDPR provisions do not apply to personal data consisting of information that the controller is obliged by an enactment to make available to the public, to the extent that the application of those provisions would prevent the controller from complying with that obligation.”

The Land Registration Act 2002 is the principal legislation governing land registration in England and Wales. It sets out provisions for the keeping of a register of title to land and requirements for its administration by HM Land Registry under a Chief Land Registrar.

The Chief Land Registrar is required by the Land Registration Act 2002 and to make register information (including any documents held on the register of title) available to the public, therefore the following data protection provisions do not apply:

  *   the requirement to provide personal data in response to subject access requests

records.transcript:
Enquiries Service
The National Library of Wales

I am researching the title history of Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr),
Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Glamorgan, adjoining St Dochdwy’s churchyard
(approx. ST 167 733).

Glamorgan Archives (Louise Hunt, ref. 2026/4097, 24 September 2026) has
confirmed that the following references are yours, not theirs, and has
directed me to you:

1. D153 — Deeds relating to premises in p. Llandough, co. Glam., comprising
a dwelling house adjoining the churchyard, 1811 (D153/1–2), and land (D153
onwards, including items sometimes cited as D153/4–8).
2. D219 — Llandough manorial leases and agreements.
3. The main Bute Estate deposit, GB 0210 BUTE (deeds to 1937; Glamorgan /
Cardiff rentals).

I do not ask you to adjudicate title. I ask only whether the following
instruments exist in your holdings, and for catalogue references, dates,
parties, acreages, and whether a plan is attached.

A. The 1877 division
Does the Bute deposit contain a conveyance, agreement, or other instrument
of about 1876–1877 by which the Marquess of Bute (or trustees) conveyed or
contracted to convey the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres adjoining
the churchyard at Llandough to Daniel Thomas (or Thomas and another), while
retaining about 9 acres of agricultural land to the east?

B. The 1916 agricultural tenancy
Does the deposit contain a yearly agricultural tenancy, or counterpart, of
1916 from the Marquess of Bute to John Williams of Great House Farm,
Llandough?
If yes:
- does the parcels clause describe the whole farm, or only the land Bute
still owned after 1877?
- is there a plan?
- what acreage is stated?

C. Rentals 1877–1936 for this farm
Do Glamorgan / Cardiff / Llandough rentals in GB 0210 BUTE distinguish,
after c.1877, between:
- a house/buildings holding (Thomas / later Williams), and
- a residual Bute field holding later passed to Western Ground Rents in
1938?

D. Anything that would show the two holdings were treated as one unit again
before 1938.

Purpose. HM Land Registry first-registered titles WA231076 (30 November
1982) and WA240304 (23 February 1983; later amalgamated). The 1982/83 files
treat the land as one farm. The family case is that Parcel A (house and
about 10 acres) had already left Bute in 1877 and was not the land let in
1916, so the 1982 merged title cannot be the same unit as the 1916 tenancy.
Your deeds and rentals are the estate-side evidence that can confirm or
deny that.

I live in Patagonia and cannot visit Aberystwyth in person in the short
term. I would be grateful for:
- catalogue references and a short description of any matching items;
- whether copies can be supplied, and the cost;
- if the 1916 tenancy is not in GB 0210 BUTE, any note of where Bute
tenancy counterparts after 1910 were deposited.

This is a new enquiry. It is not a repeat of FOI/2026/11. Glamorgan
Archives hold the 1938–44 Western Ground Rents plan/rental book (D696) and
have already answered on their own Bute material.

Requester (Requester) Buckler

[phone redacted]

https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1916-tenancy/

email.subject: Formal complaint — GGAT / Heneb: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough — HER identifiers and the 1978–1995 record

records.transcript:
Chief Executive / Complaints Officer,

This is a formal complaint to Heneb: The Trust for Welsh Archaeology, as
operational successor to the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust, and to
Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust Limited (The), company 01276976, which
remains an active company with its registered office at Heneb's address.

It concerns Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan (near
Penarth / Cardiff); ST 1681 7331; NPRN 20182. Cadw and RCAHMW have supplied
three unreconciled HER references for the same site: GGAT02038s, GGAT03586s
and GGATE003872.

This is not a chaser of my records request of 8 September 2026 or the
schedule of 19 September (ref GHF/HENEB/2026-09-20). That request remains
open and is due a response by 6 October. Please treat this complaint as a
separate file and give it a complaint reference.

What this is not. It is not an allegation that GGAT demolished the house,
advised that it be demolished, or decided that it should not be listed. It
is not an allegation of dishonesty, bad faith or criminal conduct. It is
not a title claim and I do not ask you to adjudicate BP v Buckler. GGAT's
letters of 13 and 15 December 1993, recommending a Breach of Condition
Notice when Condition 18 had not been met, were the Trust doing its
curatorial job. That is recorded here so it is not lost in what follows.

The charge, put narrowly. GGAT was the public curator of the regional
record; the adviser who told the planning authority it could not determine
89/01396/OUT without an archaeological assessment; the body which, in the
same document, specified machine-trench evaluation, quoted £2,000 and two
weeks, and recorded that it was already negotiating that work with BP
Properties; the contractor who then executed that evaluation on a
churchside monastic site its own 1978–80 excavations and its own 1982
letter had already flagged; and the author of a zoning map which treated as
empty ground in which, four years later, inhumations were found a few
centimetres below the topsoil. Disclosure of the dual role was not
management of it. The public record still does not reliably carry what was
found. Heneb's entire substantive reply since May is one sentence about
corporate form.

I enclose GGAT — Forensic Critique, Version 4.0.0 (21 September 2026). It
distinguishes established fact, reasonable inference, what cannot be
established, and facts that cut against the criticism. Where earlier
versions were wrong, the corrections are printed and kept. The critique is
the sourcing. This letter is the complaint. Please answer the letter. Treat
the critique as the schedule of sources, not as a substitute for numbered
answers.

1. I have not seen the HER

I do not assert the wording of GGAT02038s, because I have not been allowed
to read it. Cadw has said the content of the HER is managed by Heneb.
RCAHMW and Cadw have given three different identifiers for the same site.
Tests of Archwilio on 20 September 2026 did not return an error for
unresolved records. They returned a different record, from a different
trust, for a different site, with no warning:

GGAT02038s → GAT46242 (Gwynedd desk-based assessment)
GGAT03586s → GAT92911 (farmstead, Warwick Place, Gwynedd)
GGAT02038s, alternative path, three attempts → E001657 each time

A control query for an indexed record returned correctly. Please test those
three queries, correct the substitution if confirmed, and tell me the
outcome. Then permit inspection of the source file and supply an index of
every linked site and event record with its correct reference.

2. "Partially recorded" is RCAHMW's phrase, not a finding I have verified
on the HER

On 10 June 2026 Dr Adam Coward quoted NMR 6048945: "The house remained
partially recorded because of problems created by an ownership dispute. The
house and farm buildings were suddenly and completely destroyed by B. P.
Properties Ltd. on 6th December 1988 amid considerable local controversy."

That is the Royal Commission's file. I hold H. J. Thomas's measured
ground-floor plan of 26 April 1974, at 1:100, identifying the principal
rooms including the Dairy and recording the beams. GGAT reproduced that
plan as Figure 2 of its 1990 assessment, by kind permission. A measured
ground-floor survey that could not reach the first floor and roof is not,
without more, a failed survey.

Please state, from records you hold:
(a) whether the HER uses the phrase "partially recorded", and if so from
which source;
(b) what parts of the building the 1974 survey measured, and what it did
not;
(c) what contemporaneous document, if any beyond NMR 6048945, establishes
that access was restricted by the ownership dispute, by whom, on what date,
and to whom;
(d) whether Trench 7 of 1990 (north-east corner / former dairy, stone
floor, mortared partition) was ever reconciled against the 1974 plan, and
if the Trench 7 drawings, photographs and grid survive.

3. What GGAT held in 1988, and what it did not do

On 1 October 1982 GGAT told the Vale that occupation might continue north
of the church and that thorough investigative work should precede
development. Between that letter and November 1988 no GGAT act concerning
this site has been identified. RCAHMW added to its 1974 plan on 12 December
1988, six days after the demolition. There is no equivalent GGAT event. The
1990 report notes architectural features "observed in the rubble" and then
begins GGAT's own account with the words "Following the demolition… GGAT
entered into discussion with Debenham Tewson".

Please state what the SMR entry contained immediately before December 1988;
whether the 1982 advice was on it; whether any emergency building record,
watching brief on the demolition or the rubble, or post-demolition fabric
report exists; and where the carved stone and other architectural material
later referred to now is.

4. "County treasure"

GGAT 1989 §2.3: "At present our information on the Great House Farm area is
limited to the records of the recently demolished property which was listed
as a 'county treasure'." The phrase conferred no statutory protection.
Identify the list or card, the date, the criteria, and what information
about the building accompanied it. If you do not hold that document, say so.

5. Specify, price, bid, execute

In one 1989 consultee report GGAT advised that 89/01396/OUT should not be
determined without an assessment; specified machine-excavator trial
trenching; quoted two weeks at £2,000; and recorded that negotiations with
BP Properties via Debenham Tewson were already under way. BP then
commissioned GGAT. The 1990 report disclosed a "dual role" and invited
either party to go elsewhere. Disclosure is recorded. It is not the same as
management.

The IFA Code of approved practice for contractual arrangements was adopted
on 17 September 1990, after the assessment was delivered. It does not bind
that commission. The Welsh Archaeological Trusts' Code of Practice dates
from November 1997 and is not applied retrospectively. What did bind the
1989–90 arrangement, as contemporaneous standards rather than as a pleaded
cause of action: the IFA Code of Conduct in force from June 1985; the BADLG
Code, which GGAT expressly endorsed in the 1989 report; section 13 of the
Supply of Goods and Services Act 1982 as the implied standard of care
between GGAT and BP (the family was not a party); and the fiduciary duty of
charity trustees to identify and manage conflicts, not merely to notify two
commercial counterparties.

On 18 May 1994 GGAT's Curatorial Section wrote, of another contractor: "An
archaeological contractor should never be in the position of writing his
own Brief as well as carrying out the work." That principle was not met by
GGAT's own 1989–90 arrangement.

Please identify who wrote the 1989 recommendation, who accepted the
commission, whether those functions were separated, whether trustees or
Cadw were told, and who wrote the 1990 brief. If you hold Appendix "B" to
the officer's report (GGAT's further comments of 8 February 1990), Appendix
"D" (the representation from a County Councillor identified as a member of
GGAT), or Appendix "E" (the applicant's agents' written response to GGAT's
report), produce them. None of those three is in the planning file released
in 2026. Appendix "A" is. I do not assert that GGAT removed them. I ask
whether copies survive in GGAT/Heneb files.

6. The 1990 method against GGAT's own model

GGAT had excavated an early-medieval cemetery, a Roman villa and a
Tewkesbury Abbey grange immediately south of the same church, on the same
alkaline Liassic geology, and had written that occupation might continue
north of it. It chose eight machine-cut trenches, some placed "at random",
and then rated uninvestigated eastern ground "non existent to low"
potential. That rating converted a logistical limit into an empirical
claim. Cotswold's December 1994 preliminary report recorded that burials
continued into that zone and "lay only a few centimetres below the topsoil".

I do not say a 1990 evaluation had to predict 1,026 burials. I ask whether
the method was capable of detecting shallow inhumations on ground where
GGAT's own experience predicted excellent bone survival, and whether the
1990 evaluation has ever been reviewed against the 1994 results. If it has
not, will Heneb review it now.

7. Human remains and the 1981 Act

GGAT identified the Disused Burial Grounds (Amendment) Act 1981 and found
disarticulated human bone by the churchyard wall. That Act turns on whether
the land is a burial ground. A colour-coded potential map cannot answer it.
What legal advice was obtained, when, and from whom? What evidence set the
burial-ground boundary? Was a review undertaken after 1994?

8. Two burial figures, both correct

Cotswold's December 1994 preliminary report, §4.2: 858 inhumations and 152
disarticulated bone groups. Holbrook and Thomas, Medieval Archaeology 49
(2005): 1,026 burials comprising 814 articulated inhumations and 212
disarticulated bone groups, of which 801 skeletons received full
osteological analysis; "by far the largest Early-medieval burial population
so far recovered from Wales". They are the same excavation counted twice.
Please confirm which figure the HER now carries, and that both stages are
identified as such.

9. The c.1880 ironwork sentence, and what Amgueddfa Cymru now holds

GGAT 1990: "it is likely that some medieval ironwork which is held by the
National Museum of Wales was discovered under the rear wing c 1880 (RCAHMW
1988)." By 2005 that hedged sentence had become flat assertion in print.

Amgueddfa Cymru's disclosures of 25 August 2026 (FOI 2026-024 and internal
review 22 September 2026) and 22 September 2026 (FOI 2026-032) establish
the following, so far as the Museum holds recorded information:

(a) No accession, donation, transfer or deposit answering a visor, lance,
helmet, armour, soldier, horse, or nineteenth-century discovery under the
farmhouse floor.
(b) Accession 82.44H is the 1979 GGAT excavation assemblage. Collected by
Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust Ltd, 1979; donated 14 June 1982 by
Wales & West Housing Association Ltd; bibliographic reference Owen-John
1988. The collections database locality field is "Llandough Roman Villa",
NGR ST 168 733 — not "Great House Farm".
(c) Accession 95.56H is the 1994 Cotswold Archaeological Trust cemetery
assemblage. Collected by CAT, 1994; donated 28 July 1994 by Ideal Homes
Wales Ltd. Locality field: "Great House Farm Llandough", NGR ST 1681 7331.
Period on the human-remains entries: Early Medieval (c.400–c.1070).
(d) Accession 63.24 is objects stated to have been found at Church Farm,
Llandough, in 1858. The Museum's explanatory note of 22 September 2026
records that this is the only paperwork on that file, and that staff
consider it possible those objects are the basis of the later local story.
That is the Museum's observation, not a finding I ask you to adopt as fact.

Qualify or withdraw the 1880 sentence if you hold no source beyond the 1990
wording. Carry 82.44H and 95.56H on the principal HER description, with
collector, donor, donation date, locality field as catalogued, and NGR. If
the HER still points a professional user first to a post-medieval dwelling,
that is a record defect against what both excavations produced and what the
national museum now catalogues.

Please also confirm whether GGAT retained copies of the 1980 donation
correspondence with the National Museum (letters of 14 and 24 April 1980
are on the public record) and of any transfer file for 82.44H.

10. What the public record must now say

If GGAT02038s, or its successor identifier, still leads as a post-medieval
farm or dwelling, it does not satisfy the function of a working historic
environment record, and it is difficult to reconcile with section 194(2)(j)
of the Historic Environment (Wales) Act 2023. I have not seen the source
file, so I put that as a request for correction if the classification is as
described by Cadw officers, not as a finding I have verified on the face of
the record.

A professional user needs, in the principal description and not only in a
later narrative paragraph: the 1974 measured survey; GGAT's 1978–80 work
and 1982 advice; that the 1990 evaluation followed demolition and found
human bone; that the 1994 excavation recovered the assemblage above,
including in the 1990 low-potential zone; museum accessions 82.44H and
95.56H with their catalogued localities; and a note that the c.1880 NMW
ironwork attribution is uncorroborated by the institution said to hold the
object.

Please also reconcile the NGRs in use for the farmhouse, the 1990 trenches,
the 1994 excavation, the churchyard and the development parcels.
Distinguish this site from Great House Farm, Llandough near Cowbridge, and
from Llandow. Two Llandoughs sit in the same historic county. Homonym error
is a live records risk.

What I ask now

A. A complaint reference, the name of the person who will determine it, the
procedure you will apply, the timescale, and any independent review route.
Preserve all surviving Great House Farm records pending that determination.

B. Confirm which legal entity holds the records and functions formerly of
GGAT Ltd, and who handles HER corrections.

C. Answer sections 1 to 10 from the documents you hold. Where a document
does not survive, say when it left the file, under what retention rule, and
by whose authority.

D. Correct the HER so that the 1979 and 1994 investigations and accessions
82.44H and 95.56H sit in the principal description, the 1880 attribution is
qualified, the 1990 low-potential zone is annotated against the 1994
result, the three identifiers are reconciled, and Archwilio does not
silently substitute another trust's site.

E. Test and, if confirmed, correct the Archwilio substitution.

F. If you accept any part of this complaint, say what remedy you offer:
record correction, release of surviving files or an index, a written
account of the 1989–90 dual-role arrangement, and a methodological note on
the 1990 evaluation against the 1994 excavation.

I do not ask you to adjudicate title. I do ask you to account for what GGAT
knew, what it recorded, what it advised, what it then sold and executed,
what was found four years later, what the national museum now catalogues
from GGAT's own 1979 work, and whether the public record now tells the
truth of that sequence.

This letter is sent so that Heneb and GGAT Ltd have a fair opportunity to
investigate, answer, and offer remedy before any further process. Please
answer each numbered section. A general assurance that the organisation
acted appropriately will not do.

Regards,

Requester

FOI 2026-032

Enquiries Service
The National Library of Wales

I am researching the title history of Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Glamorgan, adjoining St Dochdwy’s churchyard (approx. ST 167 733).

Glamorgan Archives (Louise Hunt, ref. 2026/4097, 24 September 2026) has confirmed that the following references are yours, not theirs, and has directed me to you:

1. D153 — Deeds relating to premises in p. Llandough, co. Glam., comprising a dwelling house adjoining the churchyard, 1811 (D153/1–2), and land (D153 onwards, including items sometimes cited as D153/4–8).
2. D219 — Llandough manorial leases and agreements.
3. The main Bute Estate deposit, GB 0210 BUTE (deeds to 1937; Glamorgan / Cardiff rentals).

I do not ask you to adjudicate title. I ask only whether the following instruments exist in your holdings, and for catalogue references, dates, parties, acreages, and whether a plan is attached.

A. The 1877 division
Does the Bute deposit contain a conveyance, agreement, or other instrument of about 1876–1877 by which the Marquess of Bute (or trustees) conveyed or contracted to convey the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres adjoining the churchyard at Llandough to Daniel Thomas (or Thomas and another), while retaining about 9 acres of agricultural land to the east?

B. The 1916 agricultural tenancy
Does the deposit contain a yearly agricultural tenancy, or counterpart, of 1916 from the Marquess of Bute to John Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough?
If yes:
- does the parcels clause describe the whole farm, or only the land Bute still owned after 1877?
- is there a plan?
- what acreage is stated?

C. Rentals 1877–1936 for this farm
Do Glamorgan / Cardiff / Llandough rentals in GB 0210 BUTE distinguish, after c.1877, between:
- a house/buildings holding (Thomas / later Williams), and
- a residual Bute field holding later passed to Western Ground Rents in 1938?

D. Anything that would show the two holdings were treated as one unit again before 1938.

Purpose. HM Land Registry first-registered titles WA231076 (30 November 1982) and WA240304 (23 February 1983; later amalgamated). The 1982/83 files treat the land as one farm. The family case is that Parcel A (house and about 10 acres) had already left Bute in 1877 and was not the land let in 1916, so the 1982 merged title cannot be the same unit as the 1916 tenancy. Your deeds and rentals are the estate-side evidence that can confirm or deny that.

I live in Patagonia and cannot visit Aberystwyth in person in the short term. I would be grateful for:
- catalogue references and a short description of any matching items;
- whether copies can be supplied, and the cost;
- if the 1916 tenancy is not in GB 0210 BUTE, any note of where Bute tenancy counterparts after 1910 were deposited.

This is a new enquiry. It is not a repeat of FOI/2026/11. Glamorgan Archives hold the 1938–44 Western Ground Rents plan/rental book (D696) and have already answered on their own Bute material.

Dear Independent Complaints Reviewer,

Complaint about HM Land Registry — titles WA231076 and WA240304 (closed),
land north of Leckwith Road, Llandough (Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr). HMLR
references: N610CGV, 260919-6726246.

I ask you to review how HM Land Registry handled my complaint. HMLR gave
its final decision on 25 May 2026 that the title was "registered
correctly". I understand you cannot review that registration decision
itself. My complaint is about the way it was reached and handled:

1. The decision came before the file was examined. HMLR gave its final
decision on 25 May 2026, but did not list what the first-registration files
actually contain until 30 July 2026. A final complaint decision cannot
properly rest on documents that had not yet been identified.

2. The decision relies on a document that does not appear on the file.
HMLR's letter of 19 April 2026 described a 15-year root of title. The root
relied on, a conveyance of 31 December 1969, was under 13 years old at
first registration in 1982. Neither that conveyance nor the 1971 abstract
said to prove it appears on the 30 July 2026 file list, and HMLR has not
explained this.

3. HMLR has given three different dates for the closure of title WA240304:
1983 (file correspondence of 12 April 1983), 1987 (an amalgamation
application of 2 February 1987, made while my family's appeal was pending)
and 2005 (an email of 21 September 2026). It has not reconciled them.

4. The stage 1 response relied on a form FR1 certificate, although the
applications were on forms 1E and 1C.

5. The file holds examination material (form D23 and a letter of 8 April
1983) and two 1994 applications "to correct the title". HMLR has not
explained any of them.

6. My written questions, including through my MP Stephen Doughty, have been
redirected to a property search service instead of being answered.

The outcome I seek is a numbered written answer to these points,
confirmation that all first-registration, amalgamation and correction
records for both titles are being preserved, and acknowledgement of any
failure in how the complaint was handled.

I am separately taking advice on whether to apply to alter the register. I
understand that is outside your remit.

Yours faithfully,

Requester
